Input: n m, then m lines `u v w` meaning a directed edge u -> v with weight w (nodes are 1..n). Output n lines: line u lists node u's outgoing edges in input order as `v:w` separated by spaces (an empty line if it has none).

problems.title: Relaxation
problems.description:
Relaxing an edge u -> v with weight w means: if the path through u is shorter, update dist[v] = dist[u] + w. Dijkstra relaxes every outgoing edge of the node it expands.

Input: n, then a line with dist[1..n] (-1 means infinity), then m and m lines `u v w`. Relax every edge once, in input order, and print the new dist (keep -1 for still-infinite).

problems.title: Dijkstra (BOSS)
problems.description:
Put it all together. Input: n m s, then m lines `u v w` (directed edge, w >= 0). Print the shortest distance from s to every node 1..n separated by spaces, -1 if unreachable.

Recipe: build the adjacency list (Level 2), start with dist[s] = 0 and a min-heap holding (0, s) (Level 1), pop the closest node like the BFS loop (Level 3), skip it if the popped distance is stale, and relax its edges (Level 4), pushing any improved node back into the heap.

The Ref buttons show your own solutions to the levels you have already cleared.
